name: Clear Secured Services Limited
sector: Facility management, manpower and infrastructure services
summary: Diversified facility-services/trading special situation with a low reported earnings multiple and supported core-service growth, but weak historical cash conversion and material reporting reconciliation gaps. A funded annual model now quantifies both attractive reference returns and severe customer/collection financing downside. BQS/GQS are numerical quality estimates, while final IAS remains NS under G2; no investment ranking or buy conclusion.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Research hold, not a buy ranking. Diversified facility operations have genuine constant-parent service growth, but group expansion also includes acquired Comfort Techno and new cash-recycler trading. A fully linked forward model now shows a potentially attractive conditional reference return at ₹74, alongside severe funding and equity-loss scenarios. Persistent pre-acquisition cash weakness, customer concentration and unresolved reported cash-flow/receivable reconciliation keep final IAS NS. Disclosed promoter proceedings remain allegations, not proved misconduct. [S1–S4]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026; NSE Emerge CSSL, ISIN INE1EF801010, listed 8 December 2025. Consolidated AS statements are used, with constant-parent facility revenue explicitly separated. ₹ crore unless stated. Official 19 October close ₹74 and 24,047,112 shares imply ₹177.95 crore; neither the close nor March debt/cash is described as a live October execution/balance sheet. Five investor years end 19 October 2031, including a 202-day terminal fiscal stub. The 15% equity hurdle is an analyst assumption, not WACC. ₹5 lakh reference position, lot 1,000. Historical normalized cash confidence remains Low, while verified current face balances and bounded modeled inputs support Medium-confidence reference factors. G1/G3/G4 Conditional, G2 Hold; no proved funding default or blanket suspension. [S1–S4][MX1–MX4]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 4.42; GQS raw 5.10, capped at 5.00 for persistent CASH 3. All canonical quality factors now have company-specific evidence. REV 6 uses 12.70% constant-parent facility CAGR, not acquired group growth; BAL 4 reflects linked funding stresses. Reference R/D/P/L are 10/2/5/1. Raw IAS 5.605 is explicitly suppressed to NS by G2, and all point-score rankings remain ineligible. A high conditional R does not overcome zero modeled bear recovery or the reliability hold. Exact contributions, full coverage and cap/gate effects are in score_audit. Moving the most judgmental MOAT or CAP one point changes BQS by 0.20/0.12; it does not release G2. [E1–E16]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Facility management, manpower, security, electronic surveillance and infrastructure services coexist with CRM equipment trading, agro trading and steel manufacturing. FY26 segment revenue/result: facilities ₹415.60/₹40.91 crore; CRM ₹160.85/₹3.22 crore; agro ₹164.82/₹6.87 crore; steel ₹36.71/−₹1.43 crore. Results precede group finance and unallocated items. Payroll requires funding before client collections; equipment and commodities introduce different margins and credit cycles. Do not apply a technology or pure recurring-services multiple to the whole group.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Integrated service delivery and recurring client needs offer operating scale, but FY25 top-ten customers supplied 89.83% of sales and government entities 35.47%. Tender qualification is a capability rather than assured renewal or pricing power. The agro subsidiary depended on one client in the five months to August 2025. The prospectus names Aarvi Encon, Integrated Personnel Services and Kapston as partial peers; their FY25 EBITDA margins were approximately 2.62%, 3.83% and 4.49% in the issuer table. Their service mix differs from CSSL’s trading/acquisition mix. November 2025 peer prices are stale and are not used as October 2026 valuation anchors. Direct primary peer checks add context: Kapston reported FY26 total revenue ₹831.89 crore, EBITDA ₹45.46 crore and PAT ₹28.13 crore; Aarvi reported operating revenue ₹649.85 crore and PAT ₹17.62 crore, with explicit labour/gratuity exceptional adjustments. Their staffing mix and other-income accounting differ from CSSL. Integrated Personnel remains a partial prospectus comparator rather than an asserted current-price multiple. No peer ranking is fabricated from unmatched periods. Management’s claimed regulatory moat and sovereign payment protection are not accepted as proof of zero credit or collection risk, especially after the disclosed customer provision. [P1][P2][S5]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Comparable legacy facility-services revenue is ₹247.0926/279.1447/318.1114/353.7027 crore in FY23–26, giving a three-year CAGR of 12.70% and latest growth of 11.19%; annual additions were ₹32.0521/38.9667/35.5913 crore. This is the declared underlying REV basis, with no extra one-year trajectory adjustment. FY26 group facility revenue ₹415.5963 crore includes ₹61.8936 crore beyond the parent baseline. Group revenue of ₹777.9717 crore also contains ₹160.8453 crore new CRM trading, ₹164.8208 crore agro and ₹36.7094 crore steel. Transferring agro activity into a subsidiary is not a loss of consolidated demand, so the parent total decline is not scored mechanically. Group FY23–26 totals ₹309.0386/347.5428/476.1753/777.9717 crore remain diagnostics, not an organic CAGR. Owner PAT ₹30.2023 crore versus ₹9.9219 crore is affected by acquisition scope and the FY25 ₹8.4416 crore debtor provision. Five/ten-year growth is ND with only four relevant comparable annual observations. No subsequent unreported half-year or seasonal TTM is invented. [S1][S3][S4]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Service demand recurs, but payroll deployments, infrastructure work and trading require funded receivables, not merely order headlines. The June presentation describes 4,500+ professionals, 17-state licensing, 30,000+ ATM coverage, government backlog of about ₹142 crore phased over roughly four years and a ₹200 crore annual private contract; these are attributed management disclosures, not incremental revenue to add to the existing baseline. Project/customer schedules, cancellation rights and collections matter more than an aggregate backlog. [S5]

The March IPO monitor showed ₹8.47 crore unspent: debt object ₹2.82 crore, GCP ₹5.43 crore and issue expenses ₹0.22 crore. This is inside reported cash, not a second funding source. July 31 approved another utilization-timeline revision and surety execution without quantified terms. The model funds the residual debt object once and lets GCP cover already-modeled ordinary costs, avoiding duplicate expense/cash assumptions. Restricted deposits must grow alongside execution. FY26 normalized operating EBITDA proxy is ₹53.3012 crore after removing other income; NOPAT at an assumed 26% tax is about ₹32.96 crore. Against average equity plus debt less reported free cash, a roughly 13.4% broad capital-return proxy lies within, not clearly above, a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range. It retains collateral and committed CWIP capital; it is not a project IRR. A full acquisition-date incremental-return bridge remains limited by noncash entry/reconciliation gaps. [S1][S2][S7]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The ₹26.7987 crore loan without specified repayment terms is to wholly owned Clear Secured Ventures, carrying 12% interest. It eliminates on consolidation; it is not evidence of an unexplained external promoter advance. The funding tenor and subsidiary return remain capital-allocation questions. The annual report identifies CFO succession to Ashish Dubey from April 2026; family involvement requires oversight scrutiny, not an automatic adverse finding. The December 2025 prospectus also discloses two pending criminal proceedings involving promoter Vimal Dhar Dubey. It records his denial and quashing petitions, and states no conviction at that date. Subsequent legal status is not independently verified. Economic transmission could be tender eligibility, reputation or key-person disruption; no finding of guilt or shareholder abuse is inferred. Exact disclosed matters concern the promoter, not a criminal prosecution of the issuer: Allahabad High Court application under Section 482 No. 32090/2022 to quash Crime 191/2021 (allegations including intimidation, unlawful entry and attempted violence; promoter denies participation); and Criminal Miscellaneous Writ Petition 9301/2023 challenging action under the Uttar Pradesh Gangsters Act arising from Crime 109/2022. The prospectus describes corresponding Varanasi/Bhadohi trial proceedings and historical protection/stay orders. Its listed hearing dates are historical, not proof of a continuing stay on 20 October 2026. No complainant or unrelated family details are included.

Separately, the company’s 16 July 2026 filing approves initiating proceedings before NCLT Mumbai but does not identify the respondent, requested relief or amount. It does not establish insolvency proceedings against CSSL and is not conflated with the promoter matters above. The 31 July filing approves a further IPO-use timeline revision and surety-bond execution without quantified detail. August 21 records appointment of Nikita Jain as company secretary and a secretarial auditor, alongside routine director/AGM matters. These updates do not establish the current status of the promoter cases. [S6–S8]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Reported consolidated FY26/FY25 CFO is −₹9.6465/−₹22.4336 crore. FY26 cash-flow financing includes ₹20.2391 crore noncash consideration shares for Comfort Techno; the report explicitly includes acquired opening PPE in investing purchases and acquired deferred tax assets in other assets. Consequently, reported ₹45.9305 crore PPE/CWIP outflow is not all current-period cash capex. Opening acquired tangible PPE of ₹10.0478 crore reduces this line to ₹35.8827 crore before any other noncash adjustments. Capital reserve ₹0.9509 crore is also included in investing. A complete acquisition working-capital/opening-cash bridge is still needed; no definitive normalized FCF is asserted. Receivable and advance movements continue to indicate material funding demand independently of this classification issue. Statement CFO for FY23/FY24/FY25 is −₹1.6719/+₹0.9464/−₹22.4336 crore, establishing weakness before the new acquisition. Current and noncurrent lien deposits total ₹65.7683 crore and cannot simply offset ₹94.9217 crore debt. Note 18 identifies ₹5.9208 crore bank deposits free of lien, but total cash there is ₹20.1379 crore versus ₹20.7192 crore on the face. Receivables detail shows ₹131.6504 crore versus ₹125.8919 crore on the face, a ₹5.7585 crore reconciliation difference; original pages 107/133/134 were visually checked and exchange results support the face. The difference is not labelled stolen cash or a quantified profit overstatement. Cash-note and advance-note differences are smaller. These items require a consolidated reconciliation rather than arithmetic netting across inconsistent bases.

The forward model starts from the already consolidated March face balance sheet rather than fabricating the historical acquired opening WC. Net gratuity is ₹5.3743 crore after ₹0.2209 crore plan assets: current ₹0.7403 crore is paid once, noncurrent ₹4.634 crore retained at terminal, plus ₹0.035 crore long-term security deposits payable. Gross obligation is not deducted again. The current tax line is a net ₹0.1285 crore asset, left unrecovered outside operating WC, not an assumed tax payable. Appeal deposits ₹0.9619 crore and accrued FD interest ₹8.9572 crore are also outside WC. Ordinary statutory, employee and expense liabilities remain within the face ₹32.6159 crore other-current-liability stock, not a second settlement. The retained current OCL-versus-note difference is ₹0.7092 crore; the model does not erase it. [S1]

All ₹65.7683 crore pledged principal remains unavailable in the main case and additional collateral is cash-funded. Interest income and cash interest are separate: the reported cash-flow statement presents interest received, while accumulated-interest movements still need the acquisition bridge. Base collection of only 25% of new FD interest is an explicit conservative assumption, with 0–100% sensitivities, not an asserted historical measured rate. New unpaid interest is not automatically valued at par. Noncurrent deposits, properties, investments and old loan recoveries are not added to terminal cash without separate support. These choices bound forward funding without pretending to resolve historical normalized FCF. [S1][E13][E14]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹74, current market capitalization is ₹177.95 crore and static FY26 owner P/E 5.89×. Core operating EBITDA excluding ₹6.6088 crore other income is ₹53.3012 crore; mixed-period EV/core EBITDA is about 4.74× without netting pledged deposits. Neither metric alone establishes owner value. [S1][MX2]

The linked model replaces the old unfinanced PAT grid. Base service growth is 12%, CRM 0% then 5%, agro 8%, steel 3%; operating EBITDA margin is 6.8%, near the historical core margin, with 18% ONWC, 9% collateral requirement and 2% revenue capex plus ₹15 crore modeled CWIP completion expenditure. Completion spending is an assumption, not a disclosed remaining budget. Cash floor is ₹5 crore; borrowing costs 11.5%, new drawings accrue half-year interest, current claims are settled once and no rescue equity is assumed. Restricted principal has zero main-case terminal recovery. Five fiscal years plus a steady terminal stub align the five-year investor horizon. [E13][E14]

Bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹0.00/₹240.38/₹493.53, annualized returns -100.00%/26.57%/46.16%, and peak debt including opening ₹239.24/₹104.68/₹94.92 crore. Base 15% hurdle entry is ₹119.51, versus ₹136.40/105.07 at 12%/18%; these are assumption-dependent, not observable fair values. Base margin with a 6× multiple still yields 18.36%, but 5.5% margin and 6× gives 7.01% and peak debt ₹158.94 crore. The 3×3 margin/multiple table, WC/collateral/interest/claims sensitivities and 25% equity-issuance case link cash and dilution. A conservative 0.1% group EV deduction covers the tiny disclosed noncontrolling stakes; negative book NCI is not added to common equity. Final IAS remains NS despite the computable reference return. [E14]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Client loss or slow government/private payment forces payroll, project and collateral funding before collections. The credible bear combines weaker service/trading growth, 4.5% margin, 24% WC, 11% collateral need, ₹5.94 crore opening collection haircut and higher interest. It requires ₹239.24 crore peak debt and leaves zero modeled common equity without a rescue. The severe scenario adds a larger client shock, 32% WC, 15% collateral, reduced usable cash and ₹10 crore unspecified contingent cash stress, reaching ₹470.17 crore debt. The contingent stress is not an asserted court award or surety claim. Impairment risk is High; the decisive variable is collections relative to payroll/collateral funding, not headline sales. Contrary evidence is the existing profitable facility franchise, verified IPO funding and banking relationships, so present insolvency is not established. Legal adverse outcomes are a possible separate transmission path, not a predicted verdict. [S1–S3][S6][S7][E14]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five times and ten times ₹74 require common equity of ₹889.74/₹1779.49 crore at unchanged shares. The linked base produces ₹578.05 crore and bull ₹1186.80 crore after funding, collateral and claims. Thus 5× is possible only under demanding favorable assumptions such as the bull growth/margin/exit combination; 10× is not supported by the modeled paths. New equity reduces per-share outcomes even while funding growth; the dilution case adds proceeds and shares together. A lower exit multiple and slower collections can remove the apparent opportunity. No success probability or unsupported multibagger promise is given. [E14]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track eight company-specific items at each applicable result/filing: (1) parent facility revenue against the ₹353.70 crore baseline and 12% modeled growth, rather than consolidated acquisition additions; (2) receivable face/detail reconciliation and the ₹29.70 crore good balances overdue six months, with delayed collection tested against the 18% base/24% bear WC ratios; (3) operating cash before and after payroll/interest, not EBIT alone; (4) pledged deposits ₹65.77 crore and accrued interest ₹8.96 crore, including actual availability/collection; (5) completion of the revised IPO uses without adding unspent cash twice; (6) disclosed surety exposure, project commitments and bank covenants, before assuming new debt access; (7) acquisition/noncash CF normalization and current statutory/gratuity claims; (8) separately sourced legal status and current exchange trading conditions. A fall in the quote is not a thesis break; inability to reconcile cash or fund payroll/obligations is. [S1–S8][MX1–MX4]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. This is a cash-constrained diversified-service/trading special situation, not a verified compounder. The funded reference case offers potential return at the dated price, but the credible loss/funding path and G2 reliability hold override a favorable numerical investment classification. BQS/GQS are useful conditional quality assessments, not rank-eligible conclusions. Resolve the concrete reconciliation and funding limits before considering an investment; a low reported P/E is insufficient. Existing-holder reduce/exit advice would additionally require portfolio weight, tax and execution information.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The annual report, restated prospectus, audited exchange results, IPO monitor, July/August corporate updates and primary peer disclosures underpin the review. Source periods and accounting scope are explicit; June presentation operating/backlog claims are management statements, not verified cash or blanket credit protection. The full model starts from the March consolidated face balances and keeps known detailed-note differences visible through conservative cash inputs and sensitivities. Historical normalized acquisition CFO remains unresolved, without blocking every supported growth/quality factor. Open issues are face/detail receivables and OCL, actual FD-interest collection, unused IPO completion, surety/covenant amounts, project completion budgets and current legal status. Current tax is a net asset, plan assets are netted once, ordinary dues stay in WC, and no noncurrent employee deficit is forced into immediate cash payment. There is no generic legal clearance, unsupported live spread or invented target contribution. [S1–S8][P1][P2][MX1–MX4]

ranking_eligibility.reason: G2 reliability hold; final IAS NS even with reference factors computable. Numerical quality estimates are not rankable investment clearance.

liquidity.name: Clear Secured
limitations: Close/last is historical, not executable bid. No bid-ask spread or depth. Absent sessions must not be interpreted as no trade unless listed throughout and not missing data. Recent IPO prelisting dates are not zero trading days; use shortened sample. Series changes/multiple rows/corporate actions require issuer review. Raw turnover in INR; exit assumes constant turnover and participation, no circuits or impact.

validation.check: Both complete official CM files contain neither matching ISIN nor CSSL symbol; security listed before window, with same ISIN observed throughout. Count absent executed trading as zero for capacity, not as proof of suspension.
validation.limitations: No live spread/depth/queue assurance; circuit and concentrated trading can dominate the mathematical participation model.

GOV.reason: Disclosure of pending promoter cases and unresolved statement/note reconciliation limits confidence. Contrary evidence: no conviction disclosed; subsidiary loan is interest-bearing and eliminated, not external diversion. No G1 finding.

MOAT.reason: Large integrated-service footprint and facility profit provide operating capability. Customer concentration and competitive tenders limit pricing power; low-margin CRM/agro trading cannot inherit a service moat.

REV.reason: Constant-parent facility revenue grew 12.70% CAGR from FY23 to FY26, within the 10–15% score-6 band. The latest 11.19% service increase is consistent, not an extra upgrade. Acquired Comfort, new CRM and transferred agro sales remain separate diagnostics.

DUR.reason: Facility-management and security demand recurs, and facilities form over half of revenue. Single-client agro dependence, tender renewal and thin-margin equipment trading limit durability.

CAP.reason: Capital is committed to subsidiary funding without fixed repayment terms and a loss-making steel segment with ₹26.60 crore assets. Contrary evidence: facility segment earns ₹40.91 crore before finance/unallocated items and supports part of the capital base. No persistent CAP<=3 cap inferred.

CASH.reason: Operating conversion is weak in three of four statement years, including pre-acquisition FY23/FY25, with substantial overdue receivables. Contrary evidence: FY24 was positive and FY26 classification needs normalization, so reported FY26 FCF is not treated as exact. Structural working-capital dependence supports the persistent-cash cap.

BAL.reason: Debt of ₹94.92 crore and pledged deposits of ₹65.77 crore create financing dependence. The funded reference peak is ₹104.68 crore; the credible margin/collection stress reaches ₹239.24 crore. Verified cash, IPO debt repayment and banking relationships support the reference path. Missing covenant and surety detail limits resilience confidence, without proving insolvency.

EXEC.reason: Revenue and facility segment results expanded and Comfort integration broadened capabilities. Contrary evidence: acquisition scope obscures organic performance and financing/receivable demands persist; scale alone is not cash execution.

EARN.reason: FY25 debtor provision and acquisition accounting reduce comparability; face/note differences weaken detailed balance-sheet confidence. Contrary evidence: owner PAT and primary statement totals are readable and matched to exchange results, so no blanket null of all operating facts.

R.reason: The conditional base five-year return of 26.57% exceeds the 15% hurdle by 11.57 percentage points, mapping to R 10. Lower note cash, explicit collateral funding and 25% cash collection of new FD interest are included. Zero FD cash interest and ₹10 crore extra cash cost retain this band. G2 remains a hold and bear equity is zero.

D.reason: Customer, payroll and pledged-deposit funding link a credible lower-margin, slow-collection case to ₹239.24 crore peak debt and zero terminal common equity; severe peak debt is ₹470.17 crore. Reference cash generation and IPO funding support survival if execution and collections hold. This is a modeled adverse path, not an assertion of current default.

P.reason: At ₹74, the reference 15% hurdle entry is ₹119.51. A 6× multiple at base margin still yields 18.36%, but 5.5% margin with that multiple yields only 7.01% and raises peak debt to ₹158.94 crore. This mixed expectations buffer depends on margin and financing, not just a low P/E.

L.reason: Complete exchange files support two absent executed-trade sessions in 60. Conservative mean/median capacity implies 20.61 sessions at 5% participation. A ₹74,000 lot and explicit less-than-100-PAN and irregular-trading cautions further constrain implementation. Dated trades do exist; no suspension is inferred.

Opening cash uses lower detailed-note₹20.1379crore, not face₹20.7192. No extra IPO cash is added. ₹8.47crore monitor balance is inside cash; ₹2.82crore debt object is paid once, while GCP supports already-modeled ordinary expenses, not a second use.

Restricted principal₹65.7683crore remains unavailable in the main case. Additional collateral grows with sales; cash yield is a separate sensitivity. Terminal release0/50/100% is conditional, not double netting debt.

Current provisions/expense/statutory claims inside ONWC are not paid twice. Unknown surety and court outcomes are bounded cash stresses, not asserted obligations or accusations.
Forecast new borrowing is required funding, not committed bank headroom. Main cases assume no new equity;25% issuance sensitivity adds proceeds and shares together.

Minority stakes are tiny but nonzero; deduct0.1%of whole-group EV conservatively instead of adding negative book NCI to common equity. No extra book investment/property/loan recovery is added to the main terminal value.
